business_problem: SAP needed to reduce repetitive support demand, break down knowledge silos, and automate business processes for regulated, multilingual customers without sacrificing European data localization or trust in AI-generated answers.
solution_summary: SAP built a reusable enterprise AI framework on top of Mistral Large to support multilingual knowledge work and agentic business processes while keeping data hosted on SAP operated infrastructure in Europe. In the first deployment at Swiss Federal Railways, the team implemented a chatbot that uses retrieval-augmented generation to pull answers from FAQs, training materials, recordings, and screenshots, then applies glossary-based query rewriting so abbreviations such as "SO" are expanded before retrieval. When the bot cannot answer, human-in-the-loop escalation captures expert responses and feeds them back into the knowledge base. The service is surfaced inside SAP Build Work Zone and Microsoft Teams, and the same hosted framework is being extended to autonomous agents such as SAP's Accounting Accruals agent that reads SAP system data and policy documents to prepare draft journal entries.

solution_components.name: Mistral Large
solution_components.role: Provides the multilingual language understanding and response generation layer for SAP's chatbot and agent workflows.

solution_components.name: SAP operated infrastructure
solution_components.role: Hosts the models locally so SAP can keep data residency and sovereignty controls in place.

solution_components.name: SAP Build Work Zone
solution_components.role: Embeds the support assistant into employees' existing portal workflows.

solution_components.name: Microsoft Teams
solution_components.role: Provides a collaboration entry point for the multilingual support experience.

data_flow: FAQs, training materials, recordings, and screenshots feed a RAG knowledge base; employee questions arrive through SAP Build Work Zone or Microsoft Teams, glossary rewriting expands domain abbreviations before Mistral Large retrieves and answers, and unresolved cases are escalated to experts whose responses are written back into the knowledge base.
business_outcome: SAP's Mistral-powered framework cut repetitive support demand at SBB, scaled from a 1,000-user pilot to 30,000 employees, continuously expanded its knowledge base through expert feedback, and established a reusable path toward autonomous finance and procurement workflows for regulated industries.
metrics: 100% European, locally hosted AI, maintained in SAP-operated infrastructure.
